title: Sugar Crash on the PI3K Pathway: The First Report of Inavolisib-Associated Diabetic Ketoacidosis
content: Phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase (PI3K) inhibitors are an important targeted therapy for advanced, PIK3CA-mutated breast cancer, and hyperglycemia is a common adverse effect. However, diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is rare and has not previously been reported with the next-generation PI3K inhibitor inavolisib. We describe a 76-year-old woman with metastatic hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer and previously well-controlled type 2 diabetes who developed DKA approximately two weeks after initiation of inavolisib combined with palbociclib and fulvestrant for newly diagnosed pulmonary metastases. She presented with generalized weakness and a mechanical fall. Laboratory evaluation revealed hyperglycemia (>500 mg/dL), metabolic acidosis (pH 7.27, bicarbonate 14 mmol/L), anion gap 27, and moderate ketonuria, consistent with DKA. The patient was managed in the intensive care unit with intravenous fluids, insulin infusion, and discontinuation of inavolisib, resulting in rapid clinical and metabolic recovery. This case represents the first documented instance of inavolisib-induced DKA, highlighting the need for early glucose monitoring, patient education, and prompt recognition of hyperglycemic emergencies in patients receiving PI3K inhibitors, even those with previously well-controlled diabetes.
